title: Saving an unaccepted Petro preview publishes its zone/pay results
failure: The curve-save branch correctly substitutes accepted values under previews, but then calls _zone_results with the live working well. That function evaluates cutoffs and summaries from well.curves and well.units, including preview values, and publish_zone_values durably writes the result.
trigger: A pay definition uses a curve that is temporarily replaced by a formula preview; save the workspace/project without accepting that preview.
consequence: Map, Bubble Map and other readers can consume technical results that contradict the accepted stored curve. The result remains published until a later operation recomputes it.
evidence: The real Petro application and formula path were exercised on a temporary project. Accepted X=1 and X>0.5 gave net=5 ft. Preview X=X*0, then Save, kept canonical X=1 but changed persisted net to 0 ft and N:G to 0. Discard plus another Save restored 5 ft. See preview-zone-evidence.json.
fix: Compute published summaries from a complete accepted-state snapshot on canonical axes, including accepted units/metadata; never pass the live preview well into durable publication. Keep preview rendering separate.
tests: Preview replacing an accepted cutoff input: save, read zone results through a second connection, discard, save/reopen. Repeat with an externally edited/deleted accepted input and a preview of the manual flag itself.
coverage: test_v0939_fixes.py verifies accepted curve values/metadata and discard, not the separately published zone_values. Existing pay and zone-publication tests do not combine this preview/save boundary.
risk: Moderate: publication must share the accepted-state rule while preserving existing pay equations.

title: Mixed-unit zone publication relabels earlier values without converting them
files: database.py:2718–2751 (ProjectDatabase.publish_zone_values); petroworkbench/geo_link.py:993–1034 (_zone_results); ogmap/sources.py:193–207 and zone_attribute collection
failure: Zone attributes have one shared units field. Each publication updates that field to the incoming unit while keeping other wells' numeric values untouched. Petro produces length-valued pay summaries in each well's own depth unit; Map reads all rows using the single shared attribute unit.
trigger: Equivalent pay definitions in feet and metre wells publish into the same zone and attribute names. Both well-depth units are supported elsewhere in the suite.
consequence: Previously correct technical values acquire the wrong physical meaning. Grids, bubbles, posting and exports can mix unlike lengths while labeling them uniformly.
evidence: Actual _zone_results and publish_zone_values produced 100 ft and 30.48 m for physically equivalent all-pay zones. After the metric publication, both rows were labeled m, but their values remained 100 and 30.48. sources.collect returned those same unequal values with unit m. See zone-units-evidence.json.
fix: Establish and retain an attribute's canonical unit and convert compatible incoming values before writing, or retain per-value units and normalize at consumption. Refuse incompatible units explicitly. Do not silently relabel old numbers.
tests: Publish equivalent feet/metre results in both orders, read through Map/Bubbles and reopen, and assert equal physical values with a stable unit. Include blank and incompatible units plus phi-h/HCPT and producer ownership.
coverage: test_regional_depth_units.py covers mixed-unit top/isopach geometry and stable grid units; test_bubbles.py covers publication on a common unit. Neither exercises per-well mixed-unit publication into one attribute.
risk: Moderate: existing inconsistent attributes require explicit diagnosis/recovery; do not guess how old values were authored.

title: Seismic Rename still writes an obsolete grid snapshot
failure: Seismic loads a complete grid before displaying the rename dialog, changes its name after the dialog returns, and calls grids.save on that old object. It bypasses grids.rename, the new name-only operation that reloads under the write lock.
trigger: Another window/module regrids or changes scientific grid metadata while Seismic's Rename dialog is open; complete Rename afterward.
consequence: A presentation-only name edit can overwrite newer values, unit, notes and control/settings state with the older snapshot.
evidence: While the real rename method's dialog callback was active, a second connection changed the first grid value from 7000 to 7500, unit ft to m and notes to a new interpretation. Completing Rename retained the new name but stored 7000, ft and empty notes. The probe mocks only the dialog/render notifications; actual storage and grid files are used. See seismic-rename-evidence.json.
fix: Route Seismic Rename through grids.rename and use its returned current object; handle a deleted grid without recreating it. No storage rewrite is necessary.
tests: Exercise the Seismic entry point with an intervening save and deletion while the dialog is open; reopen and compare all scientific content. Keep the existing Geo Map rename regressions.
coverage: The v0.9.39 name-only tests cover the grids service and Geo MapWindow, not GridsMixin.rename_project_grid in Seismic.
risk: Low: use the existing tested name-only service at the remaining caller.

title: Image opacity and visibility saves can erase a newer registration
files: ogmap/window.py:2931–2963 and 3358–3365 (save_image_layer, set_image_opacity, ask_image_opacity, image visibility); ogmap/georef.py:331–344 (save)
failure: Image display commands mutate the cached ImageLayer and save the whole object, including georef. The name-only rename fix does not protect these display-only writes.
trigger: Keep the Opacity dialog open while another connection saves an image registration; then accept the opacity value. A stale cached layer can likewise be used by the visibility path.
consequence: A style edit can replace valid control points/transform/lock state with an older registration, moving the image or making it unregistered.
evidence: The actual MapWindow opacity-to-save methods were bound with rendering callbacks omitted. During the opacity dialog callback, another SQLite connection saved a valid three-point affine registration. Accepting 50% opacity wrote opacity=0.5 but removed all three points and stored an unregistered image. See image-opacity-evidence.json. The opacity failure is reproduced; the visibility path shares the same whole-object save.
fix: Add field-only persistence for opacity/visibility and call it from display commands; reserve georef.save for explicit registration edits with appropriate stale-edit checks.
tests: Opacity and visibility changes after a concurrent registration/rename must preserve all current registration data. Include deletion while a display dialog is open and reopen-based assertions.
coverage: test_map_images.py covers registration/display behavior, and test_v0939_fixes.py covers image rename preservation. No concurrent registration-plus-opacity/visibility preservation test was found.
risk: Low to Moderate: separate a few display-field updates from registration persistence without altering transforms.

title: Grid path allocation can overwrite a valid unregistered grid file
failure: _grid_path reserves paths listed in map_grids but does not reserve existing filesystem entries absent from that table. A new grid can therefore be published over a valid file already in the Grids folder.
trigger: Copy a grid into an already-open project's Grids folder, a supported register_folder workflow, then create/rename a grid to that filename before the copied grid has been registered/refreshed. Sanitized-name collisions also need preservation.
consequence: The copied grid's scientific content is replaced with no conflict prompt; a later folder scan cannot recover its original bytes.
evidence: A valid unlisted Imported.ogwgrid with first value 9000 was created in a temporary project's Grids folder. Saving a new Imported grid with first value 1000 reused that exact filename and destroyed the earlier bytes. See grid-unlisted-evidence.json. This is a file collision, not a database-corruption claim.
fix: Reserve all existing entries except the exact current grid's verified owned path; allocate a fresh collision-safe name under the save's lock/publication boundary. Keep current legitimate same-object replacement and rename behavior.
tests: Preserve valid unlisted grids and unrelated files across create/rename, including case/sanitized collisions; confirm an existing grid can still update itself and failed publication preserves both files and rows.
coverage: test_project_assets.py and test_audit_assets.py cover managed files, registered-grid collisions and failed-save rollback, not an existing unlisted destination.
risk: Moderate: path allocation must distinguish ownership from name coincidence and remain compatible with managed-file renaming.

title: Remaining CSV exporters truncate earlier completed outputs before success
failure: Both CSV writers open the chosen destination directly in write mode, then stream rows. The old file is gone if a subsequent write fails.
trigger: Overwrite a previously reviewed spreadsheet/volumetrics CSV and encounter an output error or interruption after opening it.
consequence: A useful prior export is replaced by an incomplete report despite the operation failing. Project data remains intact and the export can generally be regenerated.
evidence: With existing reviewed files, an injected OSError on the second writerow propagated but left only 8 bytes for the spreadsheet CSV and 19 bytes for volumetrics. Old bytes were not preserved. See output-failure-evidence.json.
fix: Use the existing safeio.atomic_write helper and publish the completed file only. Keep current formatting and scientific values unchanged.
tests: Fail after the header and during data rows, assert original destination bytes survive and temporary files are removed; also test successful replacement.
coverage: Existing atomic grid, seismic, shapefile and workbook export tests show the right pattern elsewhere; the two reproduced CSV paths lack equivalent failed-overwrite preservation coverage.
